title: improv·artist · haunted (Louise Bourgeois)
mutation_directive: improv artist: haunted via Louise Bourgeois

improv_extras.practice: spider, cell, charged intimate object; latex and bronze as memory

v1.feedback: The breathing membrane is a genuine interpretation of Bourgeois's cells — the contraction/expansion cycle and bruise palette land the haunted brief well. The 3D differential growth starting from a flattened ellipsoid reads as an enclosed form within ~2s, which is good. Two things to push: the interior wisps feel like filler rather than charged psychological content — replace them with fewer, slower filament traces (like stretched latex or tendons) anchored between membrane walls to evoke her fabric/bronze interiors. The tremor on membrane particles is too uniform; vary it so some regions are taut and still while others shudder, creating the psychological asymmetry that makes her cells unsettling rather than merely organic.

v2.feedback: The differential-growth membrane cell is a strong read on the Bourgeois brief — the closed curve growing outward like a distended skin, interior filaments as tendons, and the bruise-to-bone palette all land the 'charged intimate object' direction. Two things to push: the form sits flat on XZ and the camera looks slightly down at it, making it read more like a petri dish than a Bourgeois cell — tilt the growth plane or add vertical extrusion so the membrane walls rise and enclose, giving it the claustrophobic interiority of her Cell installations. Second, the spatial tremor zones are a nice idea but currently too uniform in amplitude — exaggerate the contrast so some membrane regions are dead-still latex while others convulse, selling the 'haunted' tension between containment and rupture.
